command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, time, json, sys
cmd = ["make", "verify-fast"]
start = time.perf_counter()
proc = subprocess.run(cmd)
duration_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
print("__GSD_RESULT__" + json.dumps({"command": "make verify-fast", "exitCode": proc.returncode, "durationMs": duration_ms}))
sys.exit(proc.returncode)
PY

python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, time, json, sys
cmd = ["rg", "-n", "verify-fast|verify-deep|verify", "Makefile", "README.md"]
start = time.perf_counter()
proc = subprocess.run(cmd)
duration_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000)
print("__GSD_RESULT__" + json.dumps({"command": "rg -n \"verify-fast|verify-deep|verify\" Makefile README.md", "exitCode": proc.returncode, "durationMs": duration_ms}))
sys.exit(proc.returncode)
PY
outputSnippet:
README.md:9:- `make verify-fast` is the default lane for routine changes. It runs non-E2E backend tests, Vitest, TypeScript typecheck, and the production asset build without starting the slower browser suite.
README.md:10:- `make verify-deep` runs the browser-heavy pytest E2E lane in `tests/e2e`. Use it when a change touches live enrichment orchestration, mocked online flows, results-page DOM/state, or any behavior that could accidentally trigger real background enrichment work.
